problems.constraints:
- `1 <= n <= 2000`, `0 <= edges.length <= 5000`
- no self-loops or repeated edges
problems.statement: An undirected graph has `n` nodes labelled `0` to `n - 1` and the edges in `edges`. Return the number of connected components.
problems.title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph

problems.statement:
`heights` is an island map; the Pacific Ocean touches its top and left edges and the Atlantic its bottom and right edges. Rain water flows from a
cell to a side-adjacent cell whose height is less than or equal, and from edge cells into the adjacent ocean. Return the coordinates
`[r, c]` of every cell from which water can reach **both** oceans, in any order.
problems.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow

tests.explanation: A single cell touches both oceans.

problems.statement: Return `true` if some value appears at least twice in `nums`, and `false` if every element is distinct.
problems.title: Contains Duplicate

problems.statement: Return the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray of `nums`.
problems.title: Maximum Subarray

problems.constraints:
- `2 <= nums.length <= 10^4`
- `-10^9 <= nums[i], target <= 10^9`; exactly one solution
problems.statement:
Return the indices of the two numbers in `nums` that add up to `target`. Exactly one valid pair exists, and you may not use the same element
twice. The two indices may be returned in any order.
problems.title: Two Sum

problems.statement:
An array of distinct integers sorted in ascending order was rotated between 1 and `n` times (rotating `[a0, ..., a(n-1)]` once gives
`[a(n-1), a0, ..., a(n-2)]`). Return its minimum element in `O(log n)` time.
problems.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

tests.explanation: Rotated n times: back to sorted order.

problems.statement:
Return the minimum number of intervals to remove from `intervals` so that the rest don't overlap. Intervals that only touch at a point (like
`[1, 2]` and `[2, 3]`) do not overlap.
problems.title: Non-overlapping Intervals

problems.statement:
`intervals[i] = [start, end]` is a meeting. Return `true` if one person can attend all meetings (no two overlap; a meeting may start exactly when
another ends).
problems.title: Meeting Rooms

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= nodes in root <= 2000`, `1 <= nodes in subRoot <= 1000`
- `-10^4 <= Node.val <= 10^4`
problems.statement:
Return `true` if `root` contains a subtree identical to `subRoot` in structure and node values. A subtree consists of some node and **all** of its
descendants.
problems.title: Subtree of Another Tree

problems.statement: Return the number of `1` bits in the binary representation of the positive integer `n`.
problems.title: Number of 1 Bits

problems.statement:
`height[i]` is the height of a vertical line at `x = i`. Choose two lines that, together with the x-axis, hold the most water, and return that
amount (width times the shorter height).
problems.title: Container with Most Water

problems.statement:
Return `answer` where `answer[i]` is the product of every element of `nums` except `nums[i]`. Don't use division, and run in `O(n)` time. The
products fit in a signed 32-bit integer.
problems.title: Product of Array Except Self

tests.explanation: Only the 0's position gets a non-zero product.

problems.statement: Return the length of the longest **strictly** increasing subsequence of `nums`. Aim for `O(n log n)`.
problems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence

problems.statement: Return `a + b` without using the `+` or `-` operators.
problems.title: Sum of Two Integers

problems.constraints: - `1 <= m, n <= 100`; the answer fits in a signed 32-bit integer
problems.statement:
A robot at the top-left of an `m x n` grid moves only right or down. Return the number of distinct paths to the bottom-right corner. The answer
is at most `2 * 10^9`.
problems.title: Unique Paths

problems.statement: Return the longest substring of `s` that is a palindrome. If several have the maximum length, any of them is accepted.
problems.title: Longest Palindromic Substring

problems.statement:
`nums[i]` is the money in house `i` along a street. Robbing two adjacent houses triggers an alarm. Return the most money you can rob without
robbing adjacent houses.
problems.title: House Robber

problems.statement: Return `true` if the binary trees `p` and `q` are identical: same structure and same values in the same places.
problems.title: Same Tree

problems.statement:
The `n x n` binary grid contains exactly **two** islands (groups of `1`s connected horizontally or vertically). You may turn `0`s into `1`s to
connect them. Return the smallest number of `0`s you must flip.
problems.title: Shortest Bridge

tests.explanation: The inner island is one flip away.

problems.statement:
`nums1` and `nums2` are sorted in non-decreasing order. Return the median of all their elements combined. The overall run time should be
`O(log(m + n))`. Answers within `10^-5` are accepted.
problems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays

problems.statement:
`heights[i]` is the height of the `i`-th bar of a histogram; every bar is 1 unit wide. Return the area of the largest rectangle that fits inside
the histogram.
problems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram

problems.statement: Sort the linked list in ascending order and return its head. Aim for `O(n log n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
problems.title: Sort List

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= tokens.length <= 10^4`
- each token is an operator or an integer in `[-200, 200]`
problems.statement:
`tokens` is an arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation, with the operators `+ - * /` and integer operands. Evaluate it and return the
result. Division truncates toward zero, there is never division by zero, and every intermediate value fits in a signed 32-bit integer.
problems.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation

problems.statement:
Return every distinct quadruplet `[a, b, c, d]` of elements from four different positions of `nums` with `a + b + c + d == target`. Quadruplets
with the same values count once; the quadruplets and the values within each may be in any order.
problems.title: 4Sum

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= n <= 500`, `0 <= richer.length <= n * (n - 1) / 2`
- `quiet` is a permutation of `0..n-1`; the richer relation is acyclic
problems.statement:
People are labelled `0` to `n - 1`. `richer[i] = [a, b]` means `a` has strictly more money than `b` (the information is consistent), and
`quiet[x]` is person `x`'s quietness (all distinct). For each person `x`, return the quietest person among everyone known to have at least as
much money as `x` (including `x`), where "known" follows chains of `richer` facts.
problems.title: Loud and Rich

problems.statement: Return the element that appears more than `n / 2` times in `nums` (it always exists). Aim for linear time and `O(1)` extra space.
problems.title: Majority Element

problems.statement: `nums` may contain duplicates. Return all **distinct** permutations of it, in any order.
problems.title: Permutations II

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= n <= 200`
- the matrix is symmetric with `isConnected[i][i] == 1`
problems.statement:
`isConnected` is an `n x n` matrix where `isConnected[i][j] == 1` means cities `i` and `j` are directly connected. A *province* is a group of
cities connected directly or indirectly, with no other city outside the group connected to it. Return the number of provinces.
problems.title: Number of Provinces

problems.constraints:
- the list has between `0` and `10^4` nodes
- `-10^5 <= Node.val <= 10^5`
- `pos` is `-1` or a valid index in the list
problems.statement:
Given the head of a singly linked list, find the node where its cycle begins (the first node reached twice when following `next`).

*Adapted I/O:* return that node's 0-based **index** in the list, or `-1` if there is no cycle. Don't modify the list, and try to use `O(1)` extra
memory.

**How the tests describe the list:** each test gives the node values of `head` and an index `pos`. The
judge links the last node's `next` to the node at index `pos` (0-based) to create a cycle; `pos = -1`
means there is no cycle. `pos` is **not** passed to your function.
problems.title: Linked List Cycle II

tests.explanation: The tail links back to index 1.

problems.statement:
You may repeatedly (1) move the first character of the binary string `s` to its end, at no cost, and (2) flip any single character, at a cost of
one. Return the minimum number of flips needed to make `s` *alternating* (no two adjacent characters equal).
problems.title: Minimum Flips to Make the Binary String Alternate

tests.explanation: Rotate twice to "100011", then flip two characters.

problems.statement:
Lemonade costs `$5`. Customers queue up and each pays with one `$5`, `$10` or `$20` bill (`bills[i]`). You start with no change and must give each
customer correct change. Return `true` if you can serve everyone.
problems.title: Lemonade Change

tests.explanation: The last customer needs $15 but you hold two $10 bills.

problems.statement:
`nums` has `n` elements, each between `1` and `n`. Return every number in `[1, n]` that does not appear in `nums`, in any order. Try `O(n)` time
without extra space (the output doesn't count).
problems.title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= n <= 10^5`
- `1 <= nums[i] <= n`; each value appears at most twice
problems.statement:
`nums` has `n` elements, each between `1` and `n`, and every value appears once or twice. Return every value that appears twice, in any order,
in `O(n)` time using only constant extra space.
problems.title: Find All Duplicates in an Array

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= path.length <= 100`, names are lowercase letters
- at most `300` calls
problems.statement:
Design an in-memory file system. Paths are absolute, like `"/a/b/c"`; the root is `"/"`.
- `ls(path)`: if `path` is a file, return a list with just its name; if it is a directory, return the names of its files and subdirectories in
  lexicographic order.
- `mkdir(path)`: create the directory `path`, including any missing parent directories.
- `addContentToFile(filePath, content)`: create the file if needed (with missing parent directories) and append `content` to it.
- `readContentFromFile(filePath)`: return the file's content.

Operations only refer to existing paths when they require one, and a name is never used for both a file and a directory.

**Test format:** a list of operations with their arguments; the expected output lists each operation's return value (`null` for the constructor,
`mkdir` and `addContentToFile`).
problems.title: Design In-Memory File System

tests.explanation: Content is appended; ls on a file lists just that file.

problems.constraints:
- paths are `/`-separated lowercase names; `1 <= value <= 10^9`
- at most `10^4` calls
problems.statement:
Design a file system that maps paths (like `"/leet/code"`) to integer values:
- `createPath(path, value)` creates `path` with `value` and returns `true`. It returns `false` (and changes nothing) if `path` already exists or
  its parent path doesn't exist. The parent of a top-level path like `"/leet"` is the root, which always exists.
- `get(path)` returns the value of `path`, or `-1` if it doesn't exist.

**Test format:** a list of operations with their arguments; the expected output lists each operation's return value (`null` for the constructor).
problems.title: Design File System

tests.explanation: "/c" doesn't exist, so "/c/d" can't be created.

problems.statement:
Asteroids move along a line at the same speed: the sign of `asteroids[i]` is its direction (positive = right, negative = left) and its absolute
value is its size. When two meet, the smaller explodes; if they are equal, both explode. Asteroids moving in the same direction never meet.
Return the asteroids left after all collisions, in order.
problems.title: Asteroid Collision

problems.statement:
In the grid, `0` is empty, `1` a fresh orange and `2` a rotten one. Every minute, each fresh orange next to (up, down, left or right) a rotten one
becomes rotten. Return the number of minutes until no fresh orange remains, or `-1` if some can never rot.
problems.title: Rotting Oranges

tests.explanation: The bottom-left orange is cut off.

problems.statement: `a` and `b` are binary strings without leading zeros (except `"0"` itself). Return their sum as a binary string.
problems.title: Add Binary

problems.statement:
`num1` and `num2` are non-negative integers written as decimal strings without leading zeros (except `"0"`). Return their product as a string,
without converting the inputs to integers or using big-integer libraries.
problems.title: Multiply Strings

problems.constraints:
- `2 <= number of nodes <= 10^5`
- `-10^9 <= Node.val <= 10^9`, distinct; `p != q`, both in the tree
problems.statement:
*Adapted I/O:* given a binary search tree with distinct values and the values `p` and `q` of two of its nodes, return the value of their lowest
common ancestor — the deepest node that has both as descendants (a node counts as its own descendant). Use the BST ordering.
problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree

problems.constraints:
- `0 <= nodes in each list <= 50`
- `-100 <= Node.val <= 100`; both lists are sorted in non-decreasing order
problems.statement: Merge the two sorted linked lists into one sorted list by splicing their nodes together, and return its head.
problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists

problems.statement: Return `true` if the binary tree is height-balanced: at every node, the heights of the left and right subtrees differ by at most one.
problems.title: Balanced Binary Tree

problems.statement:
Job `i` runs from `startTime[i]` to `endTime[i]` and earns `profit[i]`. Choose jobs with no overlapping time ranges (a job may start exactly when
another ends) to maximise total profit, and return that maximum.
problems.title: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling

problems.statement:
An undirected tree has `n` nodes labelled `0` to `n - 1` and the given `edges`. Rooting it at a node gives a tree whose height is the number of
edges on the longest root-to-leaf path. Return every node whose rooted tree has the minimum possible height, in any order.
problems.title: Minimum Height Trees
String to Integer (atoi)

problems.statement: `height[i]` is the height of a bar of width 1 in an elevation map. Return how much rain water is trapped between the bars after it rains.
problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
